noteRef.topicTitle: Structure and functions in living organisms

describe the functions of the nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane, cell wall, mitochondria, chloroplasts, ribosomes and vacuole

primer.text: Every cell is a membrane-wrapped bag of cytoplasm filled with specialised parts. This note names the structures this course requires and walks the function table: what the nucleus, membrane, wall, mitochondria, chloroplasts, ribosomes and vacuole each do — the pairing that 'describe the functions' questions demand.

lessons.title: Membranes, cytoplasm and the organelle idea
lessons.opening: A cell membrane separates every cell from its surroundings, and inside it the cytoplasm — a watery jelly of dissolved substances — hosts the organelles. Eukaryotic cells carry organelles such as the nucleus, ribosomes and mitochondria, each a sub-cellular structure with its own specific function. Watch the singular: one mitochondrion, many mitochondria.
keyPoints: The cell membrane surrounds the cell and separates it from the external environment.
Cytoplasm is the watery jelly holding dissolved substances just inside the membrane.
Organelles are the cell's sub-structures, each built for one specific function.
Nucleus, ribosomes and mitochondria sit in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells.
One mitochondrion, many mitochondria — the terms differ in number.

low.restatement: Membrane outside, cytoplasm inside, organelles within the cytoplasm: nucleus, ribosomes, mitochondria at minimum for eukaryotes.
low.analogy: The cell is a shopping mall: the membrane is the outer wall, the cytoplasm the concourse, and organelles the specialised shops.
low.examPointer: 'Mitochondria' plural versus 'mitochondrion' singular is a flagged trap — match the word to the number drawn.

medium.restatement: Compartmentalisation is the design principle: membranes around organelles let incompatible chemistries run side by side, which is why eukaryotic organisation supports larger, more complex cells.
medium.analogy: Separate shops mean a bakery and a fishmonger can share one mall without the smells mixing.
medium.examPointer: When asked to 'describe cell structures', list them; when asked to 'describe the functions', pair each with its job — two different questions.

check.stem: What lies immediately inside the cell membrane?

options.explanation: Walls sit OUTSIDE the membrane in plants.
The vacuole sits within the cytoplasm.

check.stem: Which word describes sub-cellular structures with specific functions?

options.explanation: The note defines organelles exactly so.

check.stem: Which organelles does the note name for eukaryotic cells?

options.explanation: Those are plant additions, not the named eukaryote trio.

check.stem: Which sentence uses the singular form correctly?

options.text: One mitochondrion contains the enzymes for aerobic respiration

check.stem: What does the cytoplasm consist of?

options.text: Water with dissolved substances in a jelly-like substance

check.stem: Name the barrier that separates a cell from its external environment.
Define the term organelle in one sentence.
check.modelAnswer: A sub-cellular structure that carries out a specific function within the cell.

check.stem: Explain why the terms cytoplasm and cell membrane describe DIFFERENT parts of the cell even though both sit at its edge region.
check.modelAnswer: The membrane is the thin barrier controlling what crosses the boundary; the cytoplasm is the interior medium where reactions and organelles sit — one governs traffic across the edge, the other fills the space inside it.

check.stem: A microscope image shows a rounded cell with no visible organelles at all. Using this note, state which microscope produced it and why finer detail would help.
check.modelAnswer: A light microscope lacks the resolution to resolve ribosomes and internal membranes, so the blank appearance says little; an electron microscope would reveal the organelles and let the cell be classified properly.

lessons.title: The structures-and-functions pairing table
lessons.opening: The function table pairs each structure with its job. The nucleus holds chromosomes; the cytoplasm hosts reactions; the membrane controls entry and exit; the wall adds support and prevents bursting; mitochondria respire aerobically; chloroplasts photosynthesise with chlorophyll; ribosomes build proteins; the vacuole stores cell sap and keeps plant cells firm.
keyPoints: The nucleus contains genetic material in the form of chromosomes.
The cell wall gives support, defines shape and prevents bursting.
Chloroplasts are the photosynthesis site and contain the light-absorbing chlorophyll.
The vacuole holds cell sap and keeps plant cells firm.

low.restatement: Eight pairings to learn: nucleus-chromosomes, cytoplasm-reactions, membrane-traffic, wall-support, mitochondria-respiration, chloroplasts-photosynthesis, ribosomes-protein, vacuole-sap-and-firmness.
low.analogy: A function table is a staff directory: match the face (structure) to the job (function) and the interview (exam question) goes smoothly.
low.examPointer: Answers that give the structure WITHOUT the function — or the reverse — earn half marks; always pair them.

medium.restatement: The functions cluster into information (nucleus), traffic (membrane), chemistry space (cytoplasm), mechanics (wall, vacuole) and energy or synthesis (mitochondria, chloroplasts, ribosomes) — grouping them makes recall robust.
medium.analogy: Sort the directory by department and any missing entry becomes obvious from the gap.
medium.examPointer: 'Prevents bursting' is the wall's extra clause that plain 'support' answers miss — include it for the full mark.

options.text: Absorbing light with chlorophyll to drive photosynthesis
options.explanation: Chlorophyll plus photosynthesis is the chloroplast pair.

check.stem: The cell wall prevents which failure mode?

options.text: Bursting when the cell takes in water
options.explanation: The wall's support clause includes preventing bursting.

check.stem: Which two structures together keep a plant cell firm and shaped?

options.text: The cell wall and the vacuole

check.modelAnswer: They are the site of protein synthesis.
Chlorophyll, which absorbs light for photosynthesis.

check.stem: Explain why a root cell functioning normally needs mitochondria but gains nothing from chloroplasts.
check.modelAnswer: Root cells sit in the dark, so chloroplasts would capture no light; their energy still comes from aerobic respiration in mitochondria, fuelled by sugars transported from the leaves.

check.stem: A new cell type is discovered with a wall, a vacuole, mitochondria and many chloroplasts. Predict where in a plant it lives and justify with two structures.
check.modelAnswer: Many chloroplasts point to light-exposed tissue such as the leaf, and the vacuole-plus-wall combination fits the turgid, supported cells of leaf mesophyll — so the cell belongs in a photosynthetic region.

glossary.definition: A sub-cellular structure that carries out a specific function within the cell.
The green pigment inside chloroplasts that absorbs light for photosynthesis.
The singular form of mitochondria; one aerobic-respiration organelle.
